About

A pharmacist and pharmacologist who became an educator — and who treats every future physician as a future educator, too.

Carolina Baraldi A. Restini is a pharmacist by training, with a PhD in pharmacology from the University of São Paulo, Brazil. She taught for nearly a decade at a Brazilian medical school — experimenting early with problem-based and team-based learning — before coming to Michigan State University as a visiting professor in 2016 and joining the College of Osteopathic Medicine faculty in 2017.

At MSU she directs the pharmacology thread of the D.O. curriculum across the college's three sites, and in 2024 she founded FIRE, the Foundry for Innovative Research and Education. Her scholarship spans two connected worlds: cardiovascular and renal pharmacology — hypertension, the renin–angiotensin system, and vascular function — and pharmacology education, from concept-based curricula to community-engaged, student-as-teacher outreach.

In 2024 she became the first MSU faculty member inducted as a Fellow of ASPET's Academy of Pharmacology Educators (FAAPE).

Pharmacology is the bridge between foundational knowledge and real-world clinical decision-making.

The idea at the centre of Dr. Restini's teaching: students should be able to reason about why a drug works — and predict its effects — rather than memorise names and side effects.

What she works on

Teaching pharmacology by concept

Concept-based curricula and the international “core concepts” of pharmacology; concept inventories that surface student misconceptions; and causal mechanistic reasoning — probing whether students can predict and explain a drug's effects, including how AI tools shape learning.

Students as teachers

Since 2020, her Substance Use and Prevention programme has sent first- and second-year medical students into middle and high schools across southeast Michigan to teach teenagers about opioids, vaping, and substance use — learning by teaching, under IRB-approved research protocols.

Heart, kidney & vessel research

A research foundation in cardiovascular and renal pharmacology: renovascular hypertension, ACE inhibition and the renin–angiotensin system, cardiac remodelling, nitric oxide signalling, and heart-failure risk in Brazilian populations.

FIRE — Foundry for Innovative Research and Education

“Advancing medical education through experiential learning, community engagement, and service-driven research.”

Founded and directed by Dr. Restini and launched at MSUCOM in 2024, FIRE integrates medical education, community-engaged research, and faculty and student development. Students serve while they learn — collecting data on health literacy and social determinants of health in schools, senior centres, and street-medicine settings, mentored from research question to peer-reviewed publication.

Projects include opioids and pharmacology in street medicine, biomedical-based diabetes education for community health literacy, and research on transportation barriers facing people experiencing homelessness in Detroit.

The journey

From São Paulo to East Lansing — a career that moved from the laboratory bench to the classroom, and then out into the community.

  1. 1998–2004

    Pharmacy and pharmacology, University of São Paulo

    PharmD and a master's (1998–2000) and PhD (2000–2004) in pharmacology at the University of São Paulo, Brazil — the start of a research career in cardiovascular and renal pharmacology.

  2. Brazil

    Nearly a decade teaching medicine

    Taught pharmacology, physiology, and clinical epidemiology at the University of Ribeirão Preto (UNAERP), working in a problem-based learning curriculum and mentoring students in a master's programme in health and education.

  3. 2016–17

    Visiting professor at Michigan State

    Arrived at MSU on a Brazilian government grant to develop a cardiovascular and renal pharmacology research project — expecting a one-year sabbatical.

  4. 2017

    Joins the MSUCOM faculty

    Became a faculty member in the Department of Pharmacology & Toxicology and pharmacology thread director for the D.O. programme, teaching osteopathic medical and PA students.

  5. 2022

    Promotion to associate professor

    Promoted to associate professor (fixed term) in July 2022 — and, since 2026, Professor.

  6. 2024

    FIRE is launched — and a national first

    Founded the Foundry for Innovative Research and Education (FIRE) at MSUCOM, and became the first MSU faculty member inducted as a Fellow of ASPET's Academy of Pharmacology Educators.

  7. 2026

    National leadership in pharmacology education

    Division Chair – Pharmacology for the NBOME National Faculty from January 2026; recipient of the ASPET Division for Pharmacology Education's 2026 Pharmacology Educators Award; and a 2026 AACOM Research Grant awardee.

Recognition

Honours for teaching, partnership, and service to the profession.

  • 2026

    Pharmacology Educators Award

    ASPET Division for Pharmacology Education — in recognition of her service to ASPET, the Division, and other pharmacology organisations.

  • 2026

    Research Grant Awardee

    American Association of Colleges of Osteopathic Medicine (AACOM), as principal investigator, for a study of a student-as-teacher, case-based clinical teaching model.

  • From Jan 2026

    Division Chair – Pharmacology, National Faculty

    National Board of Osteopathic Medical Examiners (NBOME). A National Faculty member since 2018, she contributed to the Level 1 Revision Project.

  • 2024

    Fellow, Academy of Pharmacology Educators (FAAPE)

    American Society for Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics (ASPET) — the first MSU faculty member so inducted, for exemplary contributions to pharmacology education.

  • 2023

    Distinguished Partnership Award for Community-Engaged Teaching

    MSU University Outreach and Engagement, for community-based service and research with high-school outreach.

  • 2023

    Transportation Support Award

    MSU Center for Community Engaged Learning, funding student travel to schools across southeast Michigan.
